answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one ivory-white acoustic buoy moored in open water, its sonar echo logged daily by an independent verifier. Random checks demand the holder sail to that exact buoy and ping it live within hours, and one crew cannot tend two buoys in the same sea. The mooring fee in outside money doubles per further buoy on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another real buoy, another crew, and twice the prior fee.
